street.description: Kiezdeutsch / Berlin youth — multicultural urban German, Turkish/Arabic influence.

casual_social.description: Default German B2C — duzen (informal) for under-40 audiences, witty.

professional_casual.description: German LinkedIn — siezen (formal) for B2B, light wit.

corporate_formal.description: German press, banking, legal — strict siezen, formal Hochdeutsch.

grammar_quirks: Du (informal you) vs. Sie (formal you) — strict business marker
Compound nouns can be very long (Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzung)
V2 word order — verb in second position
Modal particles (halt, eben, doch, mal) carry pragmatic meaning

code_switching_patterns.english_in_german: Moderate to heavy in tech, marketing, startups (Denglisch).
rules: Older audiences (50+) react negatively to excessive Denglisch

do_not_use: Forced 'geil' for excitement — has vulgar undertone, not always brand-safe

munich_bavaria: Servus greetings, slightly traditional, beer-culture references
